# OpenCode Super Sessions

Standalone OpenCode V2 plugin. User docs live in `README.md`. Contribution guidelines, architecture and rationale live in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Where the docs and the code disagree, the code wins.

## Boundaries

- Do not modify OpenCode or import its private Core/Server modules. Use public V2 APIs only, and check the installed types before relying on one.
- Do not publish npm releases or change user configuration without explicit authorization.
- Never commit credentials or local OpenCode state.
- Keep all `@opencode/*` dependencies pinned to the same exact version, and `effect` to the exact version that `@opencode/plugin` depends on.
- `./rpc` must stay importable by clients without loading OpenTUI.
- New host assumptions (command ids, priorities, event fields, payload shapes, API semantics, host file paths) go in `src/host/*` with a link to the host source line, and get a contract test in `test/contract` that reads the host through that accessor. See the Compatibility section of `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Invariants

Changes must preserve these. `CONTRIBUTING.md` explains the reasoning.

- Never write OpenCode's database, `cli.json` or the host's `session.json`. The plugin writes only its own key in session metadata (`super-sessions`), its plugin storage and its data directory.
- Every session metadata write goes through the write queue in `src/server/queue.ts`. `session.update({ metadata })` replaces the whole object, and other metadata keys must survive. A stored `super-sessions` value that does not parse is never overwritten.
- State shared across Locations lives on `globalThis[Symbol.for('opencode-super-sessions')]`. Exactly one process-wide event subscriber and one sweeper run.
- Only the server plugin runs `gh`, `glab` and `git`, through `src/process.ts`: no shell, the environment from `src/environment.ts`, a timeout, an output cap, and the home directory as working directory. The TUI only starts the OS URL opener in `src/browser.ts`, for http(s) URLs.
- A forge is asked only about hosts in `src/server/hosts.ts`: its `defaultHost`, `gitlab.hosts` and hosts of recognized git remotes. GitHub Enterprise tokens reach `gh` only for a host other than github.com.
- Detection never tracks refs from assistant text; those are mentions only. A bare `#N` is accepted only from user prompts, against the session's repository, after the forge confirms it.
- A dismissed ref is never added back automatically. Only explicit `agent` and `manual` links lift a dismissal.
- The plugin never makes a model request on its own. Notices to the agent are posted only from the `prompt` hook, before a steer prompt to an idle session, with `resume: false`.
- Snapshot refreshes never write session metadata; only link changes do.
- A keymap `run` that may fall through stays synchronous and returns a literal `false`.
- Archiving happens only through the TUI's or the Desktop window's HTTP client (`setArchived`), on a user action, the user's title suffix, or auto-archive the user turned on. Auto-archive never takes pinned, running or waiting sessions, or sessions the user restored from it.
- Cleanup only removes worktrees `context.worktree.list` reports, never the main checkout, always with `force: false`, and never before the user confirmed once. Unknown facts keep a worktree, keep reasons beat every rule, local changes and commits only the worktree reaches always keep, and the decision runs again on freshly read sessions and git state right before each removal.
- On a host newer than `TESTED_UP_TO` by minor or major, the plugin keeps working and warns once per version. A browser crash falls back to the built-in list; a crash in the sidebar's Work rows hides those rows.
- The TUI degrades without the server plugin, `gh` or `glab`: titles and archiving still work.

## Verification

- Run `pnpm check` before committing.
- TUI changes need a native render test that mounts the page through OpenTUI under Bun, including cold lazy-loading. Never insert raw text nodes into box renderables.
- Desktop GUI changes need a test against the built bundle through `test/gui/harness.mjs`.
- Window code (`src/gui` and every module it imports) never imports `node:*`: the app hands the window inert placeholders for Node.js built-ins.
- Package tests must exercise the packed build.
- Cleanup changes need a decision test for every rule and keep reason they touch; removal has no undo.
- No skipped placeholder tests or tests that duplicate implementation logic.

## Documentation

- English and concise. Keep the sponsor block and sentence-case headings. Do not invent badges, assets, or releases. No em dashes, and no semicolons in the README.
- The root README is user-facing only and covers what a user needs to install, use and configure the plugin. Implementation detail, development and architecture belong in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Mark planned functionality as planned.
- The README is also the npm page, so images use absolute `raw.githubusercontent.com` URLs.
- Keep the README's keys and options tables in step with `src/page/view.ts` and `src/config.ts`.

# OpenCode Super Sessions A session browser for the OpenCode V2 TUI that also tracks the pull requests and issues each session works on. It adds the browser and pull request status to [OpenCode Desktop](#opencode-desktop) too.

It replaces OpenCode's session list with a larger overlay where you can: - search sessions by title, pull request or issue, and message text - archive, restore, pin, rename, fork and delete sessions - peek into a session and come back to the list with `esc` - see each session's pull requests and issues with their state, review, CI and failed checks, from GitHub or GitLab - link any other work to a session, such as a Linear, Jira or Azure Boards item, a Sentry issue or a Slack thread - find finished work in a Done view, filled as pull requests merge and issues close - auto-archive Done sessions and remove worktrees you no longer need, if you turn it on ## Requirements - OpenCode 2.4.0 or later. - For the Desktop part, OpenCode Desktop 2.4 or later. - A [Nerd Font](https://www.nerdfonts.com/) in your terminal. A Mono variant keeps the columns aligned. The Notion and Sentry icons need Nerd Fonts 3.3 or later. - `gh` for GitHub or `glab` for GitLab, logged in (see [Forge support](#forge-support)). Without them the browser still works, without pull requests and issues. ## Install ```sh opencode plugin add opencode-super-sessions ``` Restart OpenCode, or run `opencode service restart` if it runs as a service. Then press `l` (`ctrl+x l` by default) or run `/sessions`. ## Usage `l`, `/sessions`, `/resume`, `/continue` and `/super-sessions` open the browser. `/sessions-classic` opens OpenCode's built-in list. Opened from a session, the browser selects that session and switches to the view that lists it, such as Done or Archived. `tab` and `shift+tab` switch between the views: | View | Shows | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Active | Sessions that are not archived or Done, as Pinned, Running, then one group per day of the last activity | | Done | Sessions whose pull requests are all merged or closed, or whose issues are all closed, and sessions you marked Done | | Archived | Archived sessions | | Pull requests | Every pull request tracked by a session in scope | On terminals at least 120 columns wide, a preview on the right shows the selected session's context usage, its pull requests and issues with their failed checks, and its transcript. ### Keys The footer shows the common keys, and `ctrl+/` (or `?` while the search is empty) lists them all. | Key | Action | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `enter` | Open the session | | `space` | Peek at the session. `up` and `down` switch sessions, `esc` returns to the list | | `tab` / `shift+tab` | Next or previous view | | `ctrl+a` | Switch between this project and all projects | | `ctrl+s` | Archive, or restore in the Archived view | | `ctrl+q` | Mark Done, or not Done | | `ctrl+f` | Pin or unpin. `1` to `9` open the first nine pins | | `ctrl+r` | Rename | | `ctrl+t` | Generate a new title | | `ctrl+d` | Delete, press twice | | `ctrl+b` | Fork the whole session, or from before one of your prompts | | `ctrl+l` | Link a pull request, issue or any web page by URL, `owner/repo#N` or `#N` | | `ctrl+g` | Open the session's pull request, issue or link in the web browser | | `right` | Move to the preview's Work rows. `enter` opens, `c` copies, `d` unlinks | | `f5` | Reload the selected row from GitHub or GitLab, skipping the cache | | `ctrl+y` | Archive every Done session, in the Done view | | `ctrl+o` | Settings | | `esc` | Close the browser | Rename, pin and delete follow your own keybinds for `session.rename`, `session.pin.toggle` and `session.delete`. With the mouse, a click selects a row and a double click opens it. A click on a pull request, issue or check opens it in the web browser, and a ctrl+click copies its link. Copying needs a terminal that passes ctrl+click to apps and accepts OSC 52 clipboard writes, such as Ghostty, kitty or WezTerm. ### Search Typing filters the list by session title and by pull request or issue number and title. `123`, `#123`, `pr 123` and `!12` find sessions tracking that number in any repository. `owner/repo#123` and full URLs find that exact ref. Work links match by id, such as `COR-1466`, by title, and by their full URL. A link to a page outside the trackers also matches any part of its URL. Sessions that match only in their message text appear a moment later, in an `In messages` group at the bottom. ## OpenCode Desktop The same plugin adds to OpenCode Desktop 2.4: - the session browser as a dialog. Press `cmd+shift+s` (`ctrl+shift+s` on Windows and Linux) or run "Super Sessions: Browse sessions" from the command palette. It has the same views and search as the terminal browser, and shows the selected session's context usage, work and latest messages on the right. The `preview` and `previewWidth` options apply to it too. Rest the pointer on a row to select it, or move with `up` and `down`. Click a row to open its session, or `cmd`+click it (`ctrl`+click on Windows and Linux) to open it in the background and keep the browser open. The pull request, issue and link lines under a session belong to its row. Rest the pointer on a line until it is underlined, then click to open its page. A middle click or `cmd`+click on a line opens it at once, and `alt+g` opens the selected session's main one. - a project picker in the browser's header. Click it or press `alt+p` to open a "Search projects" dialog like Desktop's own. It lists All projects, then the 12 projects with the newest activity, then "Other projects" with a count, which lists the rest by name. Each project shows its icon, its name, its full path and how many of its sessions run, with a dot for unread ones and for sessions waiting on a permission or a question. Type to filter by name, path or machine name. Names that start with what you typed come first, then names that contain it, then paths and machine names. Move with `up` and `down`, pick with `enter`, and close with `esc`. A project lists its sessions in all its worktrees and subfolders. The browser opens on the open session's project, or on all projects when you last picked All or no session is open. - "Add project" at the bottom of the picker, or `cmd+o` there (`ctrl+o` on Windows and Linux). It closes the browser and opens Desktop's own folder picker, which adds the folder as a project and starts a new session in it. With more than one machine connected, pick the machine first. - a Projects view after Pull requests, with the projects of every machine in one list, their folder, active and running sessions, and the sessions that run or wait on you under each one. Search filters and orders them as the picker does. `enter` or a click lists that project's sessions in Active, and a click on a session opens it. - sessions from every machine Desktop is connected to. The picker and the Projects view list the projects of all machines together, newest activity first. In the picker a project on another machine shows the machine's name in a small chip after its name, and in the Projects view the server icon and the machine's name after its folder. All lists the sessions of all of them, with the machine's name at the end of each row from another machine. A session opens, archives and is marked Done on its own machine. Pull request and issue status, Done and message search need the opencode-super-sessions server plugin installed on that machine. Without it, the machine's sessions still list, with a note naming the machine. Use the same plugin version on every machine. A machine on an older version still sorts its sessions into Done, but asks each session's project for it, which is slower. - the session's pull requests and issues in the session header, with their state, review and CI. `+N` opens the Super Sessions side tab with the session's work, and hides it again. - a Super Sessions tab in the side panel of every session, described below - the session's open pull request above the message box, colored by its checks and review, with a menu of its checks ### Super Sessions side tab The tab is pinned first in the side panel's tab strip of every session, so it stays there when you switch sessions. Open the side panel and pick it, choose Super Sessions from the side panel's `+` menu, or click `+N` in the session header. Drag the panel's edge to resize it, and Desktop remembers that width for this tab. Most of the tab is the open session's work, under a line such as "Work · 1 PR · 1 link" with the main pull request's state: its pull requests with review, CI, stack and failed checks, the issues they close, other issues, links and mentioned refs. It scrolls on its own when long. You can open, copy, link and unlink work there, and refresh it from GitHub or GitLab. A session that tracks nothing reads "Nothing linked" with a link action. At the bottom, under Working, are the sessions that need you, from every project on every connected machine, as Desktop's sidebar lists its own Working sessions: first those waiting on a permission or a question, then running ones, then those that finished in the last 24 hours and that you have not looked at since. Each row shows the project's icon and the session's title, then the project, a worktree or branch icon, the server icon when the session is on another machine, the status and the age. The open session's row is marked. Click a row to open its session, and the side tab stays open there when it was open here. The list updates as sessions start, stop, ask and get answered, takes at most about 40% of the tab and scrolls beyond that. Click "Working" to collapse it to its header and a count, and the tab remembers that. "All sessions…" opens the session browser. Home and new session drafts have no side panel, so the tab is only in sessions. Desktop's own session list in the sidebar stays as it is, since plugins cannot change it. Links follow Settings > Browser in Desktop: with "Open links in OpenCode" on, a pull request, issue, check or link opens in Desktop's browser beside its session, and otherwise in your default browser. Hold `shift` while clicking to use your default browser anyway. Pins, rename, delete, fork and peek are only in the terminal browser. Auto-archive and worktree cleanup run only while a terminal TUI is open, and they treat sessions open in Desktop tabs as open. Keys in the browser: | Key | Action | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `up` / `down` | Select a session | | `tab` / `shift+tab` | Next or previous view, from the search box | | `enter` | Open the session | | `cmd+enter` | Open the session in a background tab (`ctrl+enter` on Windows and Linux) | | `alt+p` | Search and pick a project | | `alt+s` | Archive, or restore in the Archived view | | `alt+q` | Mark Done, or not Done | | `alt+g` | Open the session's pull request, issue or link in the browser | | `f5` | Reload the selected session from GitHub or GitLab | | `esc` | Close the browser | The `alt` keys are the keys in those places on a QWERTY keyboard, and the browser shows the letter your layout puts there. `closeTabOnArchive` and `colors` apply in Desktop too. Desktop support uses OpenCode's experimental plugin API for the app, so an OpenCode Desktop update can break it until the plugin catches up. The terminal is not affected. ## Pull request and issue tracking A session tracks a pull request or issue when: - you link it in a prompt, as a URL, `owner/repo#N` or `#N` - the agent creates it with `gh pr create`, `gh issue create`, `glab mr create` or `glab issue create` - it is the pull request of a branch the session pushed, or one opened on the session's branch after the session started - the agent links it with the `link_work` tool, which it is told to use for work found any other way - you link it with `ctrl+l` in the browser - a tracked pull request closes it, such as with `Fixes #123` A pull request in a [GitHub stack](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/get-started/about-stacked-prs) shows its place after its number, such as `2/4`. A session lists the open pull requests of one stack in stack order, the one on the base branch first, and its merged ones after them in the same order. Links in the assistant's replies are mentions. They show in the preview and match in search, but never make a session Done. Sessions from before you installed the plugin are read for refs the first time you select, peek at or open them. "Scan all sessions now" in the settings reads every session in scope at once. A session is Done when it is idle and every tracked pull request is merged or closed after your last message. With no pull requests, its issues decide. `ctrl+q` overrides this either way. `d` on a pull request, issue or link in the preview unlinks it, and asking the agent works too. An unlinked ref is never added back automatically. The agent sees everything linked to its session each time it links or unlinks something. When you message an idle agent, a notice above your message also tells it what was linked from your messages, by you in the browser or by a closing pull request since it was last told. The notice never makes the agent answer on its own. Set `notices` to `false` to turn it off. ### Work links Work outside GitHub and GitLab can be linked by URL. Links to these services are read from the URL alone, with no login or network call, and show the id or title the URL carries: | Service | URL | | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Linear | `linear.app//issue/` | | Jira | `.atlassian.net/browse/` or a board with `?selectedIssue=` | | Azure Boards | `dev.azure.com///_workitems/edit/` or `?workitem=` | | Sentry | `.sentry.io/issues/` or `sentry.io/organizations//issues/` | | Notion | A page URL ending in its id | | Slack | `.slack.com/archives//p` | | Trello | `trello.com/c/` | | ClickUp | `app.clickup.com/t/` | | Shortcut | `app.shortcut.com//story/` | | Asana | `app.asana.com/0//` and `.../task/` | Links to these in your prompts are tracked like pull requests. Any other web page is tracked only when you link it with `ctrl+l` or the agent links it with `link_work`, which also takes the title the agent knows. Work links have no state, so they never make a session Done. Rows list them after the issues, in the same five lines. Forge state is kept in memory only: open pull requests for 2 minutes, closed ones for 15 minutes, merged ones for good. ## Configuration Options go in the plugin entry's `options`, as in the [GitLab example](#gitlab). Restart OpenCode after changing them. Unknown or invalid options turn the plugin off with a warning. | Option | Default | Description | | ------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `providers` | `["github"]` | Forges to ask: `"github"`, `"gitlab"` or both | | `ghPath` | `"gh"` | GitHub CLI command or absolute path | | `glabPath` | `"glab"` | GitLab CLI command or absolute path | | `gitlab.hosts` | `[]` | Self-managed GitLab hosts without `gitlab` in the name, such as `code.example.com` | | `scope` | `"project"` | Sessions the browser lists at first: `"project"` or `"all"` | | `preview` | `true` | Show the preview pane | | `previewWidth` | `0.4` | Preview share of the browser width, from `0.2` to `0.7` | | `rows.refs` | `true` | Show pull request, issue and link lines under each session | | `rows.groupIssues` | `false` | Join a session's issues and links on one line instead of one line each | | `titleScroll` | `"auto"` | Scroll cut titles on hover: `"auto"` follows OpenCode's `animations`, `"on"`, `"off"` | | `detect.prompts` | `true` | Track refs and tracker links from your prompts | | `detect.mentions` | `true` | Record refs mentioned in the assistant's replies | | `notices` | `true` | Tell the agent, with your next message, what was linked without it | | `search.body` | `true` | Index message text for search | | `closeTabOnArchive` | `true` | Close a session's tab when archiving it | | `archiveSuffix` | unset | Archive a session renamed to end with this text, such as `" !"` | | `autoArchiveDays` | unset | Archive Done sessions after this many days. `0` archives them right away | | `cleanup.deletedSessions` | `false` | Remove worktrees whose sessions were all deleted | | `cleanup.merged` | `false` | Remove worktrees whose pull request merged and that hold nothing the merge left out | | `cleanup.inactiveDays` | unset | Remove worktrees whose sessions had no activity for this many days | | `cleanup.doneDays` | unset | Remove worktrees this many days after their sessions became Done | | `cleanup.unchanged` | `false` | Remove worktrees of finished sessions with no commits beyond the default branch | | `colors.` | GitHub's colors | `"#rrggbb"`, or `{ "dark": "#rrggbb", "light": "#rrggbb" }` | The `colors` states are `open`, `draft`, `merged` and `closed` for pull requests, and `open`, `completed` and `not_planned` for issues. Most options can also be changed at runtime in the settings dialog (`ctrl+o` in the browser or `/super-sessions settings`). A value set there overrides the option. ### Auto-archive and cleanup Both are off by default. Auto-archive never takes pinned, running or waiting sessions, or sessions you restored. `/super-sessions undo` restores the last batch for 10 minutes. It needs an open terminal to run. Cleanup removes only worktrees OpenCode lists for the project, never your main checkout, and never with force. Removing a worktree deletes its directory, ignored files such as `.env` included. A worktree is always kept when: - a session in it is running, waiting for you, open in a terminal or a Desktop tab, or pinned - it has modified, staged or untracked files - it has commits no branch or tag contains The first removal asks for confirmation. "Run cleanup now" in the settings shows what each rule would remove before it removes anything. ## Commands | Command | Action | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | `/sessions` | Open or close the browser | | `/super-sessions` | Open or close the browser | | `/super-sessions settings` | Open the settings | | `/super-sessions status` | Check that `gh` and `glab` are installed and logged in | | `/super-sessions undo` | Restore the last auto-archived sessions | | `/sessions-classic` | Open OpenCode's built-in session list | | `/archive`, `/unarchive` | Archive or restore the session on screen | | `/archive-marked` | Archive every session whose title ends with `archiveSuffix` | ## Compatibility The plugin needs OpenCode 2.4.0 or later and is tested with OpenCode and OpenCode Desktop 2.4. On a newer minor or major release the terminal part works as usual and shows a warning once, and the Desktop part may break (see [OpenCode Desktop](#opencode-desktop)). If the terminal browser crashes, the built-in list opens instead. ## Limitations - The browser loads the 200 most recently updated sessions of each list. Search by message text reaches older ones. - Message search needs `node:sqlite` with FTS5 in the daemon. Without it, search covers titles and refs only. - Pushes made outside OpenCode, from your own terminal or editor, are not seen. - GitLab instances served under a URL path, such as `https://example.com/gitlab`, are not supported. ## Forge support `/super-sessions status` checks that the CLI of each configured forge is installed and logged in. ### GitHub GitHub works without configuration. Log in with `gh auth login`. github.com, `*.ghe.com` and hosts with a `github` label, such as `github.example.com`, are recognized. Log in to a GitHub Enterprise Server host with `gh auth login --hostname `. ### GitLab Log in with `glab auth login`, then add `gitlab` to `providers` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. The entry `opencode plugin add` wrote becomes an object: ```json { "plugins": [ { "package": "opencode-super-sessions", "options": { "providers": ["github", "gitlab"] } } ] } ``` gitlab.com and hosts with a `gitlab` label, such as `gitlab.example.com`, are recognized. List other self-managed hosts in `gitlab.hosts`, and log in to each with `glab auth login --hostname `. ### Other forges Bitbucket, Gitea, Forgejo and other forges are not supported yet. Pull requests adding one are welcome, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#providers) lists the steps. ## Uninstall Run `opencode plugin remove opencode-super-sessions` and restart OpenCode. To delete the search index too, remove `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/plugins/opencode-super-sessions` (`~/.local/share/opencode/plugins/opencode-super-sessions` by default). # Demo

A real OpenCode TUI with the plugin loaded, on fake repositories, sessions and GitHub and GitLab data, for screenshots. It never reads or writes your own OpenCode config, sessions or credentials.

```sh
pnpm demo
```

This builds the plugin and runs `node demo/start.mjs`, which:

1. wipes `demo/.state` and seeds it again (about 2.5 s), so every age stays relative to now;
2. creates the git repositories and worktrees under `demo/.state/home/src`;
3. imports the sessions with `opencode session import`;
4. starts `opencode --standalone` in `~/src/storefront`, on the session "Speed up search suggestions", which keeps running for as long as the TUI does.

Press `<leader>l` (`ctrl+x l`) to open the browser.

| Option         | Effect                                                                |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--keep`       | Reuse the existing state instead of seeding again                     |
| `--no-running` | Start on the home screen without prompting the running session        |
| Anything else  | Passed to `opencode`                                                  |
| `OPENCODE_BIN` | The `opencode` binary to run, `opencode` on `PATH` by default (2.2.7) |

It needs Node.js 24.16+, git and a terminal with a Nerd Font. The fake `gh` and `glab` are POSIX shell scripts. On Windows the plugin cannot run them, so the TUI starts but shows no pull request or issue state.

The import stamps every session with the time of the import, and no API sets the update time, so the seed writes each session's `time_updated` into the demo's database once the import server has exited. Each session also carries the plugin's history scan marker and the `closes` links the plugin would add, since a metadata write moves a session's update time to now.

Permission and question markers (`!`, `?`) are not part of the demo: they need a second live turn, and `--prompt` drives only one session.

# Contributing

Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. User documentation is in the [README](README.md). [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) lists the boundaries and invariants every change must keep, for people and coding agents alike.

## Pull requests

- Open an issue first for larger changes, so the approach is agreed before the work.
- Run `pnpm check` before pushing. CI runs it on Linux, macOS and Windows.
- TUI changes need a native render test (see [Tests](#tests)). A new assumption about OpenCode goes in `src/host/*` with a contract test (see [Compatibility](#compatibility)).

- Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/), such as `fix(tui): ...` or `feat: ...`.

A GitHub release tagged `v<package.json version>` publishes to npm through `publish.yml`.

## Architecture

### Server runtime

`src/index.ts` is the server plugin. The daemon calls its `setup` once per Location (project directory), and module state is not shared between Locations, so everything shared hangs off `globalThis[Symbol.for('opencode-super-sessions')]` (`getRuntime` in `src/server/runtime.ts`). The runtime holds the forge providers, the snapshot and branch caches, the repository resolver, the write queue, the event hub, the message index, the backfill job and the settings store. The first Location's options win; a Location with different options logs a warning once, and the change applies after a daemon restart.

The runtime belongs to one build of the code, identified by the runtime module's file URL and modification time. The host loads new code into a running daemon: a local plugin reloads when its files change, and `plugin.update` installs into a new directory that the next activation imports. Cache entries may change shape between builds, so the first Location on a new build disposes the old runtime (event subscriber, sweeper timers, message index handle) and creates its own. Locations still on the old module keep answering from their disposed runtime until the host reloads them. A build that lost the runtime never takes it back: the host sets the old module up again when the new one fails in a Location, and that setup gets a disposed runtime of its own, so the two builds never trade the subscriber and sweeper. A runtime from before this check has no `dispose` and stops only as its Locations detach.

Each Location registers its own tools, shell hook, `context` hook for the agent instruction and RPC handlers, all backed by the runtime. Invalid options register inert handlers instead, so the TUI degrades to titles only.

### Metadata and the write queue

Links live in session metadata under `super-sessions` (`src/refs/ref.ts`), as `{ v: 1, links, urls?, dismissed, done?, doneAt?, scanned?, pushed?, activeAt?, noticed? }`. `urls` holds [work links](#work-links). `done` is the user's Done mark from `done.set`, and `doneAt` is when it was set to `true`, which auto-archive counts days from. `scanned` is `{ scannedAt, lastMessageID?, pushes? }`, written once when the [history scan](#history-scan) finished the session. `pushed` lists the branches the session pushed (at most 50), which [branch pull requests](#branch-pull-requests) read; recording one is a link change, not a snapshot refresh, so it goes through the queue like any link. The server plugin's `session.update({ metadata })` replaces the whole object, so every write goes through `src/server/queue.ts`: a per-session promise chain that reads the session, applies a pure mutation from `src/refs/store.ts` and writes only when it changed. Tools, the shell hook, events and RPC all share it, across Locations. A stored value that does not parse, such as one a newer plugin version wrote, is never replaced: the write rejects and the daemon log names the session.

Every metadata write moves the session's `time.updated` (`SessionEvent.MetadataUpdated` in the host's projector), so the plugin never reads `time.updated` as activity. `activityTime` in `src/host/session-info.ts` is `max(time.created, time.busy, time.idle)`: the start and end of the latest run, which the host sets without touching `time.updated`, and which every TUI prompt and compaction moves. The list's order, day groups and ages, the tie order of search and the cleanup inactive rule read it. A session without run times (it last ran on a host older than 2.2.0, or it never ran) has only `time.updated`, so the first write the queue makes to such a session also stores the `time.updated` it is about to overwrite as `activeAt`, and `activityTime` reads that instead. A `!` command without a run moves only `time.updated`, so it counts with the next run.

`mergeLinks` dedupes by `refKey`, keeps the earliest `linkedAt`, and only moves a link up the source ladder (`agent`, `created` and `manual` above `prompt`, above `closes`, above `mention`). Only `agent` and `manual` links lift a dismissal. `dismissLink` also drops the `closes` links derived from a dismissed pull request. The rows and the preview list an issue a pull request closes only while a link stores it: the pull request's snapshot keeps listing an issue the user unlinked, and a waited `buildViews` (`refresh`, the sweep, the tools) stores a `closes` link for every other one before it answers. `refs` is a read and never writes: it shows the same links (`withCloses` in `src/server/links.ts`) without storing them, since every write moves the session's `time.updated`.

### Work links

A work link is a URL outside the forges: `{ url, source, linkedAt, title? }` in `urls`, with `source` one of `agent`, `manual` and `prompt`. `recognizeLink` in `src/refs/work-link.ts` reads a URL with no network call: a recognizer per tracker (Linear, Jira, Azure Boards, Sentry, Notion, Slack, Trello, ClickUp, Shortcut, Asana) returns the provider, an id unique within it, and when the URL carries them, a short id for the rows and a title from the slug. Any other http(s) URL is a generic `url` link keyed by host, port, path and query. The URL is stored without credentials or fragment, and one longer than 2000 characters once encoded is refused, so the stored value always parses. Keys start with `link:`, so they share `dismissed` with forge refs without colliding. The provider, key and title are derived on every read, so a recognizer added later applies to stored links; a key it changes must stay stable from then on, and `dismissalKeys` also checks the plain-link key a URL had before its recognizer, so a link the user unlinked stays out.

`mergeWorkLinks` follows `mergeLinks`: dedupe by key, earliest `linkedAt`, source only moves up, and only `agent` and `manual` lift a dismissal. A given title replaces the stored one, and only the newest 50 links are kept. Prompts link tracker URLs only (`trackerLinks`); generic URLs come from `link_work` and the `link` RPC, and assistant text never adds a work link. A URL of a forge that is turned off is refused instead of stored as a plain link, which would duplicate the ref once the forge is on. Work links have no state, so they never decide Done, and the Pull requests view ignores them. Older plugin versions read a value with `urls` as unparseable and so never overwrite it.

When the agent should call `link_work` is said once, in the `context` hook text (`instructionText` in `src/server/tools.ts`), which names what is linked automatically for the enabled forges and the `detect.prompts` setting. That text never lists the session's links, so it stays the same on every request and the prompt cache holds. The tool descriptions only say what the tools take.

`src/server/linked.ts` formats what the agent reads about the session's links:

- Every `link_work` and `unlink_work` result names what it linked, unlinke

The browser (`src/page/page.ts`) claims the host's `app` slot, which renders after the route inside the main column, and draws an absolutely positioned overlay only while open, so the route underneath stays mounted. While open it pushes the `super-sessions` keymap mode, which turns off the prompt and every other `base` layer, and its layer sits in that mode at priority 1. The model (`src/page/model.ts`) outlives the overlay: it caches both lists for 30 seconds, reloads 500 ms after session events while open, and keeps query, view, selection and scroll in `storage.memory`. The cache is keyed by the resolved list scope (`all`, or the project scope `projectScope` gives), so opening over a session in another worktree of the same project keeps the cached lists on screen; only a different scope resets them. When the directory under the browser no longer resolves, such as a worktree the cleanup removed before a restart, `location.get` fails and the scope comes from the session's stored project and subpath (`sessionScope`), with RPCs sent through the home Location. A load from empty data (`load` in `src/page/state.ts`) holds the lists back until their refs and Done lookups are in, for at most 400 ms, so a cold open draws once; a reload over lists on screen keeps them there and holds its new lists for their refs and Done lookups the same way, for at most 400 ms, so the rows change in one publish; a forge `refresh` publishes its refs together with the Done lookups they call for, and clearing a search that is already clear publishes nothing. The Done lookups are one `done.facts` RPC for every candidate. The Desktop window passes `hold: 0` and draws the titles as soon as the lists answer.

The Pull requests view builds its rows in the TUI from the lists and refs the model already loaded (`pullRows` in `src/page/state.ts`), so it costs no extra call. Its selection is a pull request key (`memory.pull`), and `memory.selected` follows it as that pull request's newest session; `model.rows()` is then the list of those sessions, so `enter`, `space`, the peek keys and the way back from a peek work unchanged. The session preview's Work section and the sidebar ask `pull.details` too, through `createFailedChecks` in `src/work-row.ts`, but only for open pull requests with checks to list by name (`hasListedChecks` in `src/page/checks.ts`: a failed count above zero on GitHub, a failing pipeline on GitLab), and again when their check counts change. The server's details cache absorbs the repeats, so the list never triggers a details request. `workStatus` draws the review, thread and failed check lines from that answer: the icons and a column of checks sit side by side in one row, so the first check shares the icons' line and the others line up under it, and the CI icon drops out once a check is listed.

List rows react to the pointer in `src/page/view.ts`: `hoveredRow` holds the row under it and only tints the row (`hoverBackground` in `src/page/row.ts`), which loses to the selection and the delete confirmation. OpenTUI reports no double clicks, so `clickRow` treats two left mouse-ups on the same row id within 400 ms as one. Every link the plugin draws goes through `clickLink` in `src/link.ts`, which opens it with `openUrl` or, with ctrl held, copies it with the renderer's OSC 52 support.

### Takeover and classic fallthrough

A global layer at priority 1 (`OVER_HOST`) registers commands with the host's own ids: `session.list` (slash `sessions`, aliases `resume` and `continue`) and `session.quick_switch.1` to `9`. Reusing the ids makes the user's keybinds, the slash names and the palette entries reach the plugin first. A keymap `run` falls through to the next layer only when it returns a literal `false`, and a returned Promise counts as handled, so these runs stay synchronous. `/sessions-classic` dispatches `session.list` with the argument `classic`, for which the takeover returns `false` and the built-in list opens.

### Peek

The peek keys live in a separate global layer at priority 2 (`OVER_PROMPT`). The prompt's history layer registers at priority 1 on every cursor move, so a priority 1 layer lost `up` to it. `esc` is enabled while the peeked session is on screen and no host dialog is open; `up` and `down` only in the `base` mode, and they return `false` while the focused prompt holds text. The route follows the peek cursor after 150 ms. The banner renders in the `session.composer.top` slot for the peeked session only. A user item in `session.inbox.enqueued` or any route change ends the peek.

A crash in the browser's render or key actions closes it and opens the built-in list (`fail` in `page.ts`). A crash in the sidebar's Work rows hides those rows through their own error boundary (`installSidebar` in `src/sidebar.ts`), so it never reaches the host's slot boundary, which would toast it in the middle of the session.

### Settings stores and RPC

The dialog rows are in `src/settings/definitions.ts`. TUI settings live in `context.storage.store('settings')` (`src/settings/store.ts`), read reactively, so a change applies at once in every TUI. Server settings go over the `settings.get` and `settings.set` RPC methods to `src/server/settings.ts`, which persists them under the `settings` key of the server plugin's storage and notifies the runtime; `runtime.options` applies them, and a provider change rebuilds the forges. In both stores the plugin options are the defaults, overrides equal to a default are dropped, and each stored key is parsed on its own, so a schema change loses only that key.

## Compatibility

The `@opencode/*` pins only fix the types and the tests. At runtime the plugin runs inside whatever `opencode` the user installed, so everything it assumes about the host lives in `src/host/*`, one file per area, each linking the host source it mirrors:

- `keymap.ts`: command ids the takeover reuses, the `dialog.select.*` ids the settings dialog registers, layer priorities, keymap modes.
- `events.ts`: where prompt text, assistant text and `!` commands sit in events and in stored messages (`storedHistory` for the history scan), the index keys shared with the backfill, and the last user message in a `session.context` that starts at the latest compaction.
- `tool-hook.ts`: the shell tool's name and its `execute.after` payload.
- `session-api.ts`: forking and the prompts a fork can start before, the project scope of the list for a Location, notices. It re-exports `session-info.ts`, which holds what the Desktop GUI may import too: archiving and title regeneration over HTTP, the project scope of a stored session, the list filters and the whole-project filters of the Desktop rail, the running test, the unread rule, the activity time.
- `gui.ts`: the `./gui-experimental` export and `features.gui`, the `session.header` slot and the `session.panel` menu, the layout key of a side panel tab, how `layout.open` and `hide` treat a pinned tab, the side region's open state per session tab, `tabs.open`, `tabs.list` and `tabs.close`, the app's own server, the sidebar's machine icon and row label, the app's home directory rule, the window's shell and island surfaces, and the markup and metrics of the app's text input, button, "Search projects" dialog and server chip, segmented control, session search rows and the sidebar's Working shelf that the browser and the side tab reproduce, the session search's relative times, the shelf's ages and worktree rule, the project picker's key, and the add-project flow and its keybind.
- `worktree.ts`: worktree listing and removal without force.
- `files.ts`: paths of `cli.json`, the host's `session.json` and the plugin's data directory.
- `theme.ts`: the dialog surface and backdrop, the session view background and the markdown styles.
- `tui.ts`: the slot names (`app`, `session.composer.top`, `sidebar.content`) and the focused editor's text on the renderer.
- `rpc.ts`: the `type` and `data` of an RPC error a handler returned, `rpc.unavailable` for a server without the server plugin, and `rpc.method_not_found` for a method an older server plugin lacks.
- `git.ts`: how the plugin runs git next to the agent.
- `compat.ts`: `TESTED_UP_TO` and the untested-version check.
- `forms.ts`, `permissions.ts`: the events of questions and permission requests waiting on the user.

Each assumption and what checks it:

- The `session.list` takeover through a priority-1 layer, with `false` falling through to the built-in list: the smoke test (`<leader>l` opens the browser) and a unit test (`false` for `classic`).
- The peek keys at priority 2 beat the prompt history layers: the smoke test (the arrows move the peek with an empty prompt).
- The `app` slot overlay sits under host dialogs, which take the keys: the smoke test (ctrl+r renames from inside the browser).
- The `session.composer.top` slot input `{ sessionID }`: the smoke test (the peek banner shows for the peeked session).
- Event payloads, and the keys live indexing shares with the backfill: contract tests.
- The shell tool name and the `execute.after` payload: a contract test with a real agent shell call. That a background call reports `metadata.status: 'running'` there is not checked against a host.
- `session.update({ metadata })` replaces the object, and `session.get` returns metadata and location: a contract test.
- A metadata write moves `time.updated` but not `activityTime`, with run times and with the `activeAt` stamp, and a prompt moves `activityTime`: a contract test.
- Archive and restore over HTTP, and an empty title regenerating it: contract tests.
- `session.fork` with `before` leaving that prompt and everything after it out, without it copying the whole session, the `session.forked` event (a fork publishes no `session.created`, so the browser's lists reload on this one), and the `type` filter holding across `message.list` pages: a contract test. The host's `/fork` also carries the picked prompt into the new session's composer through its route; the plugin route has no field for it, so `ctrl+b` in the browser does not.
- `message.list` shapes, paging and the `type` filter: a contract test. The same test and the `!` command test read the prompt, the agent's shell call with its output, the answer and a `!` command through `storedHistory`. That a background shell call records `metadata.status: 'running'` is not checked against a host.
- `session.list` filters and cursors: a contract test.
- A permission request's `permission.asked` event names its id and session, its reply's `permission.replied` names the request, and both reach the subscriber of another Location: contract tests. That an interrupted request publishes no reply, and that a run's `session.execution.started` comes before its tool calls ask, are read from the host source, not checked: `permission.assert` takes no signal, so only an agent run interrupted in the middle of a tool call that asks would show it.
- The worktree list marks the main checkout, and removal without force refuses local files: a contract test.
- Every agent request carries the plugin's tracking instruction once: a contract test.
- The RPC error shape: the configured-host integration fixture reads real `link` errors through `rpcError`.
- The listing with `features.gui`, the bundle `plugin.gui` serves with the plugin's options, `rpc.unavailable` for an RPC id no plugin registered and `rpc.method_not_found` for a method the plugin lacks: contract tests.
- The Desktop slot and menu ids, the panel tab key, pinned tabs and the side region's state, the `tabs` API, the plugin's declared icons, the app's own server, the machine icon and row label of the sidebar, the home directory rule, the app's surfaces, markup and metrics the GUI reproduces, the relative times, the shelf's ages and worktree rule, the picker's key and the add-project flow through `layout.project`: not checked against a host; only the desktop app renders them.
- The `sidebar.content` slot, the `dialog.select.*` ids, the dialog backdrop, the unread rule and the compaction rule: not checked against a host. A unit test covers the compaction rule on hand-written messages.
- The `cli.json` and `session.json` locations: not checked against a host. They are host files the plugin only reads, with defaults when missing.
- Markdown styles and theme surfaces: the typecheck and the native TUI tests on the latest packages in `compat.yml`.
- `gh` and `glab` output: fixture unit tests. A real check needs credentials.

`.github/workflows/compat.yml` runs weekly and on demand against the latest `@opencode/*` release, the OpenTUI version its `@opencode/theme` pins and the `effect` version its `@opencode/plugin` depends on. It installs those versions and the matching `@opencode/cli` in the runner without committing, runs the typecheck, unit, integration, contract, native TUI and Desktop GUI tests, and keeps going after a failure so the report lists every suite. A failure opens or comments on the issue "Compatibility with OpenCode <version>"; a pass writes the tested versions to the job summary.

At runtime, `TESTED_UP_TO` is the pinned `@opencode/plugin` version, read from package.json, so a Dependabot bump that passes CI raises it. On a host newer by minor or major, the TUI keeps every key and says once per version that the release is untested, so a user who hits a break knows the likely cause; holding the takeover back made every host release need a plugin release first. Patch releases, and versions that are not `major.minor.patch` such as `local` source builds, count as tested. The `untestedHosts` option is still accepted, so older configs load, and has no effect. A crash in the browser closes it and opens the built-in list; a crash in the sidebar's Work rows hides them.
